meta.title: MTG rules engine fixtures: interaction tests, loop detection, deck heuristics
meta.source: Deck analysis sessions (Vraska, Jyoti, Bumbleflower, Vren, Helga, Thranduil)
meta.schema_note: Field names are a best guess and not yet mapped to the project's ADL schema. Adapt 'setup'/'expect' keys to match the engine's game-state model.

confidence_levels.high: Card text verified during analysis and the rules interaction is standard.
confidence_levels.medium: Reasoning is sound, but the exact ruling or card text should be checked before treating it as ground truth.
confidence_levels.verify: Depends on card text or rulings not verified in these sessions. Check before use.

interaction_tests.title: Borrowed ability self-references point to the new holder
interaction_tests.action: Activate Greenhilt Trainee's ability via Thranduil.

expect.thranduil_has_ability: {T}: Target creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn. Activate only if this creature's power is 4 or greater.

interaction_tests.reasoning: Thranduil has all activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard. 'This creature' in a granted ability refers to the object that has it (Thranduil), not the card in the graveyard.

interaction_tests.title: Thranduil + Devoted Druid + Greenhilt Trainee (graveyard) = infinite mana and power
sequence: Put -1/-1 counter on Thranduil: untap (Devoted Druid ability)
interaction_tests.reasoning: Each two-step cycle spends 2 counters (−2 toughness) and gains +4 toughness plus 1 mana. The power stays ≥ 4, so the Greenhilt restriction keeps passing.
interaction_tests.caveat: The +4/+4 boosts end at cleanup and the −1/−1 counters remain, so Thranduil dies at end of turn unless the counters are offset (see THR-05).

interaction_tests.title: Thranduil + Devoted Druid + Immaculate Magistrate (graveyard) = infinite, and Thranduil survives

expect.counters: Permanent +1/+1 counters outpace −1/−1 counters; opposite counters cancel in pairs (see THR-06).

interaction_tests.reasoning: Magistrate: {T}: put a +1/+1 counter on target creature for each Elf you control. With N ≥ 2 Elves, each tap-pump nets N−1 permanent toughness after its untap counter; alternating with the Druid mana tap still nets at least 0 toughness plus 1 mana per round.

interaction_tests.title: Mana-cost pumps need a mana multiplier (Iridescent Blademaster)
interaction_tests.reasoning: Blademaster: {3}{G}: +2/+2 until end of turn. Each pump buys 2 untaps. Infinite when 2 × mana_per_tap > 4, i.e. mana_per_tap ≥ 3.

interaction_tests.title: Until-end-of-turn pumps expire; counters remain
interaction_tests.reasoning: Continuous effects that last until end of turn end during cleanup; counters persist. Then state-based actions put the creature into the graveyard (commander may go to command zone).

interaction_tests.title: +1/+1 and −1/−1 counters cancel in pairs
interaction_tests.reasoning: State-based action removes N of each when a permanent has both kinds.

interaction_tests.title: Imperious Perfect + Intruder Alarm + any mana Elf = infinite Elves and mana
sequence: Pay {G}, tap Imperious Perfect: create 1/1 Elf Warrior
Token enters: Intruder Alarm untaps all creatures
interaction_tests.variant: Imperious Perfect in the graveyard with Thranduil on the battlefield also works; Thranduil holds the token-making ability.

interaction_tests.title: Tapping other creatures as a cost ignores their summoning sickness
interaction_tests.reasoning: Summoning sickness only restricts a creature's own {T}/{Q} abilities and attacking. 'Tap ten untapped Elves you control' can use newly created tokens. Lathril itself needs to be free of summoning sickness because its cost includes {T}.

interaction_tests.title: Borrowed {T} abilities obey the holder's summoning sickness
High Perfect Morcant triggers once per Elf, including simultaneous entries

setup.event: Morcant and 2 other Elves enter at the same time

expect.effect_per_trigger: each opponent blights 1 (puts a −1/−1 counter on a creature they control)

interaction_tests.reasoning: Official ruling: if Morcant enters with other Elves, its ability triggers for each of them and itself.

interaction_tests.title: Type-restricted mana can pay for borrowed abilities on an Elf source

expect.Eclipsed Realms (Elf chosen): may pay for any ability Thranduil borrows (Thranduil is an Elf source)
expect.Woodland Weavemaster: may pay for Elf spells and abilities of Elf sources, including Thranduil's borrowed abilities

interaction_tests.title: Color-restricted sacrifice costs
interaction_tests.reasoning: Ayara requires 'another black creature'. Mono-green combo pieces are not legal sacrifices for her.

interaction_tests.title: Graveyard setup is not 'dying'

expect.note: Library-to-graveyard, discard, mill, and surveil moves do not fire 'dies' triggers or 'would die' replacements.

interaction_tests.title: Vren's replacement only applies to opponents' creatures dying on the battlefield
interaction_tests.reasoning: 'If a creature an opponent controls would die, exile it instead' only modifies battlefield-to-graveyard moves for creatures.

interaction_tests.title: Vren dying in the same board wipe still exiles opponents' creatures

setup.event: Wipe destroys Vren and opponents' creatures simultaneously

expect.count_for_end_step_rats: yes, if Vren returns before end step

interaction_tests.reasoning: The replacement effect applies because Vren is on the battlefield when the event would happen.

interaction_tests.title: Given tokens die immediately under M.O.D.O.K. and become Rats

expect.opponent 1/1 token: enters with 0 toughness (−1/−1 from M.O.D.O.K.), would die, is exiled by Vren

interaction_tests.title: 'Dies' triggers don't fire for exiled creatures
interaction_tests.reasoning: Opponents' creatures are exiled instead of dying, so 'whenever a creature an opponent controls dies' never triggers.

interaction_tests.title: Rat tokens with Vren out survive Night of Souls' Betrayal
Copies of spells are not cast
interaction_tests.reasoning: Copying a spell doesn't cast it, so 'whenever you cast' abilities ignore copies (Sword of Wealth and Power copies, storm copies).

loop_detection.model: Treat each activated ability as a resource transform: inputs (mana, tap, counters/toughness) → outputs (mana, untap, toughness, tokens). A loop is infinite when the net change in every consumed resource is ≥ 0 and at least one resource grows.

rules.description: Untap costs 1 toughness (−1/−1 counter). Pump costs C mana for +T toughness. Each tap makes M mana.
Pump uses a tap (not mana). Alternate pump-tap and mana-tap; each round spends 2 untaps (2 toughness).
Token creation triggers an untap of the token maker.
rules.infinite_when: Mana produced per untap cycle ≥ token ability cost

post_loop_checks: Do until-end-of-turn effects leave the holder dead at cleanup?
Does the loop produce a win condition (drain, blight, damage) or only a resource?
Which pieces can be disrupted mid-loop (graveyard hate, instant removal)?

deck_heuristics.note: Judgment guidelines for a deck analyzer, not rules. Treat as defaults the user can override.

user_preferences.wipe_rationale: Wipes are the catch-up button when behind; the value is higher when the commander's engine survives (e.g. graveyard-based).

redundancy.principle: Redundancy matters in 100-card singleton. Count a card as a backup only for roles it actually performs in this deck.
redundancy.example: Ayara is a backup for 'sacrifice to draw' but not for 'put green Elves in the graveyard' (black-only sacrifice).

bracket_signals: Tutor density (e.g. Entomb, Buried Alive, Dina's Guidance, Fauna Shaman)
Earliest turn a combo can realistically assemble
playgroup_notes: Deliberately low removal can be a design choice to vary play experience across decks.
